gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow's own comparison table marks the DELTA 3 Classic (the card ChatGPT priced at $462 at Best Buy and $502.88 at Home Depot) as not expandable, while the 1,024 Wh DELTA 3 and the DELTA 3 Plus take 1–5 kWh of extra battery. Anker lists the C1000 Gen 2 (ChatGPT's top pick) as not expandable, so it is limited to its one 1,024 Wh battery (about 35 minutes at 1,500 W).
standout_why: I compared against keeplights.com/guides/can-a-power-station-run-a-microwave (cited), powerstationtips.com/articles/how-long-power-station-run-microwave/ (cited) and outletpowered.com/best/1000wh-power-station/ (cited). KeepLights doesn't cover expansion and mentions X-Boost only for the RIVER 2 Pro. PowerStationTips says only 'the DELTA 2's expandability'. Outlet Powered already says the C1000 Gen 2 is not expandable and the DELTA 3 Plus goes to about 5 kWh, but it lists the DELTA 3 Classic as 'Not stated' and doesn't cover the plain DELTA 3. That split, and EcoFlow's explicit 'NO' for the Classic, is the new part. unpluggedwatts.com returned a certificate error, so I couldn't compare against it.
decides: This confirms the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 for inverter headroom: 2,000 W, the most of the three I sourced. It also shows that neither it nor the DELTA 3 Classic can go past roughly 35 minutes of 1,500 W cooking per charge. A shopper who wants more microwave time should buy the EcoFlow DELTA 3 (1,024 Wh, not the Classic) or the DELTA 3 Plus and add an extra battery. The cheaper Classic cards ChatGPT showed can't be expanded. Separately, ChatGPT's $998 price for the BLUETTI AC180 at BLUETTI-US is the two-unit option; a single AC180 is $499.
